options.option_text: Use the policy's freezer range for every refrigerator medication.
options.original_rationale: Refrigeration and freezing are different storage conditions.

questions.question_stem: The pharmacy's refrigerator has a valid temperature log and appropriate design. A planned electrical shutdown will interrupt power overnight, but no arrangement exists to preserve refrigerated drug stock elsewhere. Under Massachusetts Board Policy 2020-05, what is specifically missing?

options.option_text: Maintain a backup plan protecting refrigerated medicines during power failures.
options.original_rationale: The policy requires a backup plan for power failure or other unforeseen event.

options.option_text: Another thermometer reading from the last normal workday.
options.original_rationale: A historical normal reading does not replace a power outage backup plan.

options.option_text: A DEA Schedule II perpetual record entry for every vaccine in the refrigerator.
options.original_rationale: Refrigeration continuity does not automatically make noncontrolled vaccines Schedule II substances.

options.option_text: A manufacturer's automatic authorization to extend every drug's expiry by 30 days.
options.original_rationale: An outage does not automatically justify any product's extended dating.

questions.question_stem: A pharmacy receives returned refrigerated medication with verified temperature excursion beyond its labeled storage range. A technician suggests adjusting the expiration date by one day and placing it back on saleable stock. What is the best response?

options.option_text: Release because it is still before the manufacturer's printed expiration date.
options.original_rationale: An expiration date presumes compliant storage; excursion must be assessed.

options.option_text: Quarantine, evaluate stability evidence and document the decision before release.
options.original_rationale: The storage and cold-chain obligations require a defensible integrity assessment, not an arbitrary relabel.

options.option_text: Replace the temperature logger but keep the product without review.
options.original_rationale: Changing monitoring equipment cannot establish suitability of exposed drug.

options.option_text: Assume every excursion necessarily makes a product safe at 24 hours.
options.original_rationale: Stability impact depends on the preparation and exposure.

questions.question_stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy monitors vaccines with a digital refrigerator probe. The probe displays appropriate temperatures, but the pharmacy has no laboratory calibration-testing certificate and never follows the manufacturer's recommended recalibration schedule. What policy-specific corrective action is required?

options.option_text: Treat the display's precision as proof of accuracy without external calibration.
options.original_rationale: A displayed decimal does not replace the policy's calibration-certificate requirement.

options.option_text: Use a certified calibrated thermometer and follow its recalibration schedule.
options.original_rationale: Board Policy 2020-05 §VII requires a documented calibration-testing certificate from an accredited laboratory.

options.option_text: Measure temperature only when a vaccine shipment is unpacked.
options.original_rationale: The policy also requires routine monitoring and review of every cold-storage unit.

options.option_text: Use a household kitchen thermometer in place of a certified temperature probe.
options.original_rationale: An uncertified consumer thermometer is not an equivalent documented control.

questions.question_stem: A pharmacy delivers filled prescriptions to an employer's designated worksite collection desk under a compliant Massachusetts worksite program. The collecting employee leaves early, and the pharmacy delivery agent proposes leaving undelivered medication in the worksite office overnight. What should happen?

options.option_text: Leave the medication in a locked worksite drawer for pickup tomorrow regardless of the pharmacy's agreement.
options.original_rationale: The worksite collection rule does not permit routine overnight storage of undelivered prescriptions at the site.

options.option_text: Give the undelivered items to an unlicensed coworker who recognizes the patient's name.
options.original_rationale: Recognizing a name is not sufficient for a lawful handoff.

options.option_text: Return undelivered prescriptions to the pharmacy through its authorized collection/delivery process.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.04(9) requires undelivered medications to return to pharmacy custody.

options.option_text: Record the drugs as administered at the worksite so the chain of custody is complete.
options.original_rationale: Dispensing and administration are different events; documentation cannot invent an administration.

questions.question_stem: A pharmacy begins a home-delivery program for Schedule III and Schedule VI prescriptions. The manager argues that FDA labeling and the courier's standard service agreement replace any pharmacy written procedure. What remains specifically required?

options.option_text: No written policy because couriers own the delivery vehicle.
options.original_rationale: Pharmacy responsibility is not discharged by using a courier.

options.option_text: Maintain written policies for controlled-drug delivery, packaging and transport.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.02(3) specifically requires these pharmacy controls.

options.option_text: One universal DEA Form 222 for every Schedule III and Schedule VI package.
options.original_rationale: Form 222 is for registrant ordering of Schedule I–II, not patient delivery of these products.

options.option_text: A patient must travel to the pharmacy to sign all delivery records in person.
options.original_rationale: The law does not categorically prohibit authorized home delivery.

questions.question_stem: During the same delivery route, a courier leaves a refrigerated injection at a locked door without confirmation and sends another patient's medicine to the wrong address. Which separate pharmacy risks need to be assessed? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

options.option_text: Temperature exposure, drug stability, and chain-of-custody for the unattended injection.
options.original_rationale: Delivery cannot be judged only by possession of a shipping tracking number.

options.option_text: Confidentiality, recipient identity, and whether the other patient's medicine can safely be recovered or replaced.
options.original_rationale: Wrong-recipient delivery raises privacy and product integrity issues.

options.option_text: Both products may automatically be returned to saleable stock when the courier retrieves the boxes.
options.original_rationale: The products must be assessed for delivery status and integrity before any disposition.

options.option_text: Documentation, incident response and whether any applicable breach notification standard is triggered.
options.original_rationale: Proper response requires determining the facts and applicable reporting standards, rather than assuming none apply.

questions.question_stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy operates a lawful workplace prescription delivery and collection program. A company employee asks to obtain a prescription for a friend who does not work at the company and does not live with the employee. No other lawful patient agent authorization exists. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.option_text: The worksite program's special collection service does not extend to this unrelated friend.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.04(9) limits qualifying worksite recipients; separate proper patient-agent authorization would need review.

options.option_text: All friends of any employee are covered whenever the courier arrives at the workplace.
options.original_rationale: The special workplace collection rule has defined eligible people.

options.option_text: The pharmacy may transfer any other person's prescription into the program without checking the actual recipient.
options.original_rationale: A service contract does not waive recipient eligibility and dispensing safeguards.

options.option_text: Only Schedule II medications may be delivered in a worksite program.
options.original_rationale: The provision is not a Schedule II-only collection rule.

questions.question_stem: An overnight network outage requires a Massachusetts pharmacy to process urgent, otherwise valid prescriptions through its contingency workflow. The computer returns the next morning, but the manager wants to discard all paper records without updating the electronic patient profiles. What is required?

options.option_text: Discard all downtime records once the computers reboot.
options.original_rationale: A downtime process must reconcile dispensed medication into the electronic records.

options.option_text: Back-enter downtime prescriptions and document the appropriate DUR.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.19(22) includes continuity, record reconciliation and DUR procedures.

options.option_text: Stop all pharmacist clinical review for the entire outage.
options.original_rationale: The downtime policy must include an appropriate drug utilization review.

options.option_text: Recreate the dispensing labels from memory and omit the date of each supply.
options.original_rationale: Record integrity requires accurate entries rather than undocumented reconstruction.

questions.question_stem: A pharmacy completes a major renovation and appoints a new Manager of Record in the same week. The owner proposes doing the next Board self-inspection at the annual renewal six months later. Which statements apply? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

options.option_text: Conduct an applicable self-inspection within seven days of the renovation or MOR change.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.19(21) lists both events as triggers.

options.option_text: Annual inspection alone always replaces event-triggered inspection.
options.original_rationale: An annual minimum does not waive the seven-day event requirement.

options.option_text: Use a Board-approved inspection tool appropriate to the pharmacy's operations.
options.original_rationale: The rule specifies applicable routine and compounding tools.

options.option_text: Retain the completed self-inspection tool for at least two years.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.19(21) includes the retention period.

questions.question_stem: The last pharmacist locks a Massachusetts retail pharmacy that is inside a supermarket. Management plans to switch off the pharmacy alarm because the outer supermarket is still open. What does 247 CMR 9.21 require?

options.option_text: Turn off the pharmacy alarm because the store has customer service staff.
options.original_rationale: The pharmacy must activate its own security system when closed.

options.option_text: Leave the secured prescription area unlocked for cleaning staff.
options.original_rationale: Access and physical pharmacy security must remain controlled.

options.option_text: Keep the pharmacy prescription area separately locked and alarmed when closed.
options.original_rationale: 247 CMR 9.21(3),(5) requires an activated alarm and separate secured area.

options.option_text: Only protect Schedule II inventory; all other pharmacy controls may be unlocked.
options.original_rationale: Pharmacy controlled substances and secure prescription areas have broader requirements.

questions.question_stem: After flooding disables a Massachusetts pharmacy computer, a delivery includes an unreconciled Schedule II shipment and a refrigerated product that exceeded its labeled temperature range. The pharmacy is open under its downtime policy. Which plan best meets the distinct responsibilities?

options.option_text: Dispense everything once the courier signs a delivery ticket.
options.original_rationale: A delivery signature does not resolve inventory discrepancies or medication stability.

options.option_text: Hold all future dispensing indefinitely with no continuity procedure.
options.original_rationale: A pharmacy downtime policy must address appropriate lawful filling and continuity of care.

options.option_text: Change the temperature log and reset the controlled-stock balance without investigation.
options.original_rationale: Falsifying records and bypassing reconciliation are inconsistent with record and security duties.

options.option_text: Quarantine stock, reconcile Schedule II inventory and use downtime controls for safe dispensing.
options.original_rationale: The combined regulations require separate inventory, storage-integrity and continuity-of-care controls.
